title: Select [LIKE]
description:
Another important term in `WHERE` for `SELECT`s is `LIKE`. `LIKE` in where is used like this:
```sql
WHERE column LIKE string
```
The string you can pass can contain 3 things: Normal string, `_`, and `%`. `%` means any number of characters and `_` means one character, so "%" would mean any string of charecters, and "_" would be any singular character.
---
## Assignment:
BWS needs to find all servers whose name starts with 'prod'. Use LIKE to find them.
setupCode: CREATE TABLE servers (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, name TEXT, cpu_cores INTEGER, status TEXT); INSERT INTO servers VALUES (1, 'prod-1', 8, 'running'), (2, 'prod-2', 16, 'running'), (3, 'staging-1', 4, 'stopped'), (4, 'dev-box', 2, 'on fire'), (5, 'production-main', 8, 'running');
starterCode: -- Find all servers whose name starts with 'prod'
expectedOutput:
id | name | cpu_cores | status
1 | prod-1 | 8 | running
2 | prod-2 | 16 | running
5 | production-main | 8 | running
